Eric Hall retained his title, winning by 34 sec. from 2nd claim member George Williams who had travelled up from Worcester (that's enthusiasm).

The individual title went to Ken Matthews, Royal Sutton Coldfield, who won easily from George Meadows of Highgate and Williams of Ilford. Packing well, our lads put their team in the first twelve positions with Ted Smith 7th, Dave McMullen 8th, George Checkley 9th, Syd James 11th and Bob Newson 12th!

For various reasons we were without Eric Hall, George Williams, John Knifton & Ray Hall, so we were well under strength. The 'A' team finished 10th, with Ray Middleton 6th (97.04), Ken Bailey 32nd (109-13), Cyril Yescombe 33rd (109-27), and George Bates 44th (111.24); 111 finished.
Williams and Potlinger were more than equal to the occasion and won the Shot and Long Jump respectively. Roger Hudson also deserves credit for his 220 and 440 running.
Then came Williams and Middleton to hog the limelight. It was almost like a procession of music-hall names---rumour has it that Morecombe and Wise even considered joining our walking section.
SHORT STAGES: Geoff North, O'Hara, Williams, Bicourt, Dance, Major,. With Black, Dabbs, Steer, Buxton, Dear and a host of others itching to get in, the lads should really be on their Mettle.
4 x 110: 1.BELGRAVE H (Hamilton, Bent, White, Williams) 49.3 MATCH RESULT:- 1.BELGRAVE H 64pts, 2.Ealing & Southall 26pts.

With a host of others just getting into the stride of the track season (Thresher 13:40.4/3m, Williams 4:12.7/1m, Geoff North "This year I'll hit the top or do nothing at all", etc.) I think we can look forward to what could be a vintage year for Belgrave.
Geoff North, far from his best, brought us in sixth on the first stage on which Williams of Woodford Green ran away from the field to produce a new stage record and give his club a 44 seconds lead.
Are we doomed to hover on the fringe eternally or can runners like Major, Bicourt, Piotrowski, Williams etc give us a lift up into the medals next year?.

Alan Lerwill helped Middlesex towards the retention of their Inter-County title by clinching second place in the long jump with a 24'-3¼" leap that pushed Lynn Davis's protegé Williams back into third position.
In a tremendous tussle for third place with Williams and Scott he was beaten by a mere ½" (24'-1", 24'-1", 24'-½") yet he had the best second jump and two hair-line fouls at 24'-5".
